parts.gloss: we will not (negative first-person plural suffix)

literal: If it sees, the blue water-lily, having drooped, the ground will look at, 'the eyes of her who wears excellent ornaments we do not equal' saying.
translation: If the blue water-lily could see, it would droop its head and look down at the ground, saying, 'We can never equal the eyes of this beautifully adorned woman.'
modern: நீலக் குவளை மலர் பார்க்கக் கூடுமானால், 'சிறந்த அணிகலன்களை அணிந்த இவளுடைய கண்களுக்கு நாம் இணையாக மாட்டோம்' என்று கூறி, தலைகவிழ்ந்து தரையைப் பார்க்கும்.
explanation: In this verse, the lover praises the extraordinary beauty of his beloved's eyes. He personifies the blue water-lily, a flower traditionally compared to beautiful eyes in classical poetry. He suggests that if the flower possessed the power of sight, it would realize its own inferiority to her eyes. Overcome with shame, the lily would droop its head and stare at the ground in defeat.
